description:
Use this when an agent needs Bitcoin data. For the current Bitcoin price (BTC/USD, btc price), start with kind="intuitive" (the default; also get_bitcoin_price): a multi-source price with a Data BitScore. kind="price" is a cheaper single-source quote; kind="price_lite" is a rough whole-dollar price; kind="price_fresh" is a tighter 10 s quote. Fees and mempool are kind="oracle"; ecosystem stats kind="pro"; sentiment kind="signals". Returns JSON in the `data` field with source attribution. Read-only; the only side effect is the payment you choose to make.
Kinds and prices:
- kind="intuitive": 2 sats or $0.002 USDC. Use this for the current Bitcoin price (BTC/USD, btc price) when a wrong quote costs money and one source is not enough: sizing or approving a trade, settling an invoice in USD, or any decision a bot cannot take back. Returns a BTC price checked across independent sources, with confidence, agreement, spread, source age and outliers excluded.
- kind="price": 10 sats or $0.01 USDC. Use this when a trading or treasury bot needs the BTC spot price, a user asks "what is BTC at?", you must price an invoice in USD, or you want to flag a >2% 24h move (a 60 s quote is enough). This is a single-source price. Not BitScored; for a multi-source price with a Data BitScore, use btc_intuitive. Returns price_usd, price_eur, change_24h_percent.
- kind="price_fresh": 30 sats or $0.025 USDC. Use this when a stale quote costs money: sizing a trade, converting sats to USD at checkout, or confirming a price just before settlement. Returns price_usd, price_eur, change_24h_percent, age_seconds (cached 10 seconds at most, vs 60 seconds for btc_price). MCP: get_btc_data(kind="price_fresh")
- kind="price_lite": 2 sats or $0.002 USDC. Use this when you only need a rough whole-dollar BTC price (display, sanity check, cheap valuation). Returns price_usd as an integer, refreshed every 5 min; no EUR or 24h change. The cheapest BTC price. MCP: get_btc_data(kind="price_lite")
- kind="oracle": 50 sats or $0.05 USDC. Use this when an agent needs a Bitcoin network snapshot: choosing a transaction fee (fast, average, slow sat/vB), checking mempool congestion, hash rate, difficulty or block height, plus the BTC price. Returns market, on_chain, fees. MCP: get_btc_data(kind="oracle")
- kind="pro": 100 sats or $0.10 USDC. Use this when researching or monitoring the Bitcoin ecosystem: everything in kind="oracle" plus Lightning capacity, channel and node counts and daily miner revenue. Returns market, on_chain, lightning, mining. MCP: get_btc_data(kind="pro")
- kind="signals": 200 sats or $0.20 USDC. Use this when a trading or research agent needs sentiment and trend context: Fear & Greed index, BTC/gold ratio, % from all-time high, momentum score, volatility regime, 24h transactions (dominance, NVT and active addresses are null: no licensed source). MCP: get_btc_data(kind="signals")
Payment: call without a credential to get payment_required (isError=true) with a Lightning invoice, macaroon and, if enabled, x402 terms (USDC on Base). Pay it yourself (this server never pays), then repeat the identical call with l402_credential='<macaroon>:<preimage_hex>' (HTTP equivalent: Authorization: L402 <macaroon>:<preimage>; single use, valid 10 min), x402_payment / params._meta['x402/payment'], or credit_token (prepaid, see buy_credits). Invalid input is rejected before any invoice. Copy-pasteable examples: https://api.bittuitive.ai/pay. Informational only; not financial, investment, legal or tax advice; provided as-is, with no warranty; verify before acting. https://api.bittuitive.ai/disclaimer.

credit_token.description: Prepaid token (btf_..., from buy_credits). Pays this call from your prepaid sats or USDC balance with no invoice; a failed call is refunded. Balance is non-refundable.

kind.description: Product to fetch. Every kind, its price and when to use it are listed in the tool description. Defaults to "intuitive" (recommended Bitcoin price, BTC/USD).

l402_credential.description: L402 credential '<macaroon>:<preimage_hex>' from a paid invoice (or an active subscription). Omit it on the first call to receive the Lightning invoice and macaroon.

x402_payment.description: x402 payment (USDC on Base): base64 PaymentPayload signed for accepts[0] of the payment_required result. Alternative to l402_credential; also accepted in params._meta['x402/payment'].
